reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Counting C as all slices without weighting.
Measuring A and B on different slices.
Mixing mm and cm (result 1000 times off).
name: Intracerebral Haemorrhage Volume (ABC/2)

version.label: ABC/2 ellipsoid estimate (Kothari et al. 1996)
version.detail: Volume (mL) = A × B × C / 2, with A, B and C in cm. C = number of slices showing haematoma × slice thickness, counting a slice as 1 if its haematoma area is ≥75% of the largest slice, 0.5 if 25–75%, and 0 if <25%.

purpose: Estimates intracerebral haematoma volume on CT at the bedside.
intendedPopulation: Patients with spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage on non-contrast CT.

calculatorNotice.title: Measure on the largest slice
calculatorNotice.message: A is the largest diameter on the slice with the largest haematoma area; B is the largest diameter perpendicular to A on the same slice; C is the vertical extent.

inputDefinitions.label: A: largest diameter
inputDefinitions.help: On the axial slice with the largest haematoma area.

inputDefinitions.label: B: largest diameter perpendicular to A
inputDefinitions.help: On the same slice as A.

inputDefinitions.label: C: vertical extent
inputDefinitions.help: Weighted number of slices × slice thickness in cm (see version note).

resultStates.label: {fixed(total, 1)} mL
resultStates.detail: Volume is one predictor of outcome; correlate with location, GCS, IVH and age.

resultStates.label: {fixed(total, 1)} mL
resultStates.summary: Estimated haematoma volume of 30 mL or more (the ICH Score volume threshold).
resultStates.detail: Volume is one predictor of outcome; correlate with location, GCS, IVH and age.

clinicalContext.text: A quick bedside estimate of haematoma volume, an important predictor of outcome and expansion.
ICH volume ≥30 mL scores a point in the ICH Score.

clinicalInsights.text: Volume ≥30 mL contributes 1 point to the ICH Score.
Repeat on follow-up CT to quantify expansion.

limitations.text: Overestimates irregular or lobulated haematomas (e.g. on anticoagulation) compared with planimetry.

limitations: Slice weighting for C is often omitted, which overestimates volume.

confounders.effect: Not included in the parenchymal estimate.

guideSections.what: An ellipsoid approximation of haematoma volume: A × B × C / 2.
guideSections.whenToUse: Initial and follow-up CT in intracerebral haemorrhage.
guideSections.howToPerform: On the slice with the largest haematoma, measure A and the perpendicular B. Count slices with haematoma using the 1 / 0.5 / 0 weighting and multiply by slice thickness for C. Enter in cm.
guideSections.clinicalContext: One input to severity scores such as the ICH Score.

sources.citation: Kothari RU, Brott T, Broderick JP, et al. The ABCs of measuring intracerebral hemorrhage volumes. Stroke. 1996;27(8):1304-1305.

components.label: B: largest diameter perpendicular to A
